Track pinned tool versions in workflow env vars

packageRules.description: Automerge everything short of a major once the required checks pass. The required checks are shellcheck, hadolint and the PR image build, so this merges only after the image has actually been built on the PR and in the merge queue — the deliberate trade for zero dependency toil.
Keep first-party and base OCI images fresh immediately. The base namespaces are the three the Containerfile documents: Fedora, CentOS and Hummingbird.

Hold quay.io/fedora-ostree-desktops/* at its currently pinned major. The repository tags every active branch — `43`/`44` (released), `45`/`46` (pending) — and the docker versioning parses all of them as version candidates, so a cross-major pin would jump to an unreleased release the build has not been validated against. Disable the major outright, the same way the Ubuntu rule below does, rather than filtering with allowedVersions, whose regex/range syntax does not enforce a major ceiling here. The pin/digest bumps within the pinned major still automerge from the rule above.

Third-party GitHub Actions (everything except first-party projectbluefin/** and Homebrew/actions, which the rule below keeps separate) are safe to automerge once their release is three days old. The three-day minimumReleaseAge is the review window that #305 asked for and that #645 confirmed: a compromised update has time to be spotted before it lands, while the project still sheds its daily dependency toil. First-party projectbluefin/** actions stay automerged immediately.

Homebrew/actions tracks an unversioned moving branch and is digest-pinned to its main, so every bump imports whatever that branch holds. Renovate does not automerge it (the "automerge": false stays), and it is kept out of the three-day minimumReleaseAge rule above. The hive still merges these PRs once the required checks pass, because mergeraptor is a trusted bot and its verdict is only advisory — that is accepted, because this action only runs in validate-brewfiles.yml, which is read-only and carries no secrets. This rule sits after the digest rule above so it wins for Homebrew/actions.

Hold the build runner at Ubuntu 24.04: projectbluefin/actions' setup-runner asserts ubuntu-24.04 when adding its resolute apt source, so 26.04 fails the build. Disable the major outright rather than filtering it with allowedVersions, whose range does not parse under the docker versioning a github-runner dep uses. Drop this once upstream supports 26.04.
A major crossing always waits for a human — never automerge one. Last matching rule wins, so keep this rule last.
